question: A 65-year-old man on warfarin for atrial fibrillation requires emergency laparotomy. His INR is 5.2. Which blood product most rapidly reverses warfarin anticoagulation before surgery?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: FFP does reverse warfarin but is slow (large volume required) and is second-line to prothrombin complex concentrate for emergency reversal.

answers.text: Prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC) combined with intravenous vitamin K

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. PCC rapidly replenishes factors II, VII, IX and X (the warfarin-sensitive factors) and provides near-immediate reversal. Concurrent IV vitamin K provides sustained effect over the following 24 hours.
Warfarin affects coagulation factors, not platelet count; platelets will not correct an elevated INR.
Cryoprecipitate is used for fibrinogen replacement and haemophilia A; it does not address the factor II/VII/IX/X deficiency from warfarin.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the indications for each blood component: FFP (multiple factor deficiencies), PCC (warfarin reversal), cryoprecipitate (fibrinogen/FVIII), and platelets (thrombocytopaenia/dysfunction).
Well done. PCC + IV vitamin K is the standard of care for emergency warfarin reversal.
